nodes.summary: A subgroup $M$ of a group $G$ is minimal non-nilpotent if $M$ is not nilpotent but every proper subgroup of $M$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Minimal non-nilpotent subgroup

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal in $G$ when $H = G$ or there is a chain of subgroups $H = H_0 < H_1 < \cdots < H_n = G$ in which every index $|H_i : H_{i-1}|$ is a prime number.
nodes.title: $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal subgroup

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Schmidt subgroup when $H$ is not nilpotent but every proper subgroup of $H$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Schmidt subgroup

nodes.summary: There exist a finite group $G$ and a subgroup $H$ of $G$ with $HM = MH$ (as sets of products) for every minimal non-nilpotent subgroup $M$ of $G$ such that the quotient $H/H_G$ is not nilpotent, where the normal core $H_G$ is the largest normal subgroup of $G$ contained in $H$.
nodes.title: Permutability with minimal non-nilpotent subgroups does not force a nilpotent core quotient

nodes.summary: The statement that if $H$ is a subgroup of a finite group $G$ with $HM = MH$ (as sets of products) for every minimal non-nilpotent subgroup $M$ of $G$, then the quotient $H/H_G$ is nilpotent, where the normal core $H_G$ is the largest normal subgroup of $G$ contained in $H$.
nodes.title: Subgroups permuting with all minimal non-nilpotent subgroups (Kourovka 17.56)

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a partition of the set of all primes into nonempty pairwise disjoint blocks, and let $G$ be a finite group in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\sigma$-subnormal. Then $G$ has a normal $\sigma$-nilpotent subgroup $N$ such that $G / N$ is cyclic: there is $g \in G$ such that every $x \in G$ satisfies $x g^{-k} \in N$ for some integer $k$. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 19.85 in the affirmative.
nodes.title: Finite groups with $\sigma$-subnormal Schmidt subgroups are $\sigma$-nilpotent-by-cyclic

nodes.summary: The statement that for every partition $\sigma$ of the set of all primes into nonempty pairwise disjoint blocks and every finite group $G$ in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\sigma$-subnormal, $G$ has a normal $\sigma$-nilpotent subgroup $N$ such that $G / N$ is cyclic: there is $g \in G$ such that every $x \in G$ satisfies $x g^{-k} \in N$ for some integer $k$. The problem is due to A. N. Skiba.
nodes.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 19.85

nodes.summary: Every finite group in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal is soluble. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 18.30 in the affirmative.
nodes.title: Finite groups with $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal Schmidt subgroups are soluble

nodes.summary: The statement that every finite group in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal is soluble. The problem is due to A. F. Vasil'ev, T. I. Vasil'eva and V. N. Tyutyanov.
nodes.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 18.30

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
